task.description:
Re-check REQ-197's design (lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md) after CODE-DESIGNER's rework iteration 1, which addresses the single BLOCKER from the prior Step 1b FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/step-01b-code-design-validator.json, now overwritten by this re-request -- see git history for the FAILED verdict text if needed) plus two non-blocking flagged items. Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-197 entry in full yourself before validating -- do not trust this summary alone.

What changed since the FAILED pass:
1. BLOCKER FIX -- §4.5 (retitled 'REVISED, rework iteration 1', old text described as superseded rather than silently deleted, per this project's established convention -- see how REQ-192's design doc handled its own rework for the pattern): eval/2's ordering-comparison clause (< <= > >=) now specifies a NEW nil-check guard inserted immediately ahead of the existing is_number(lv) and is_number(rv) guard at expr.ex:437-446 -- a nil operand there now returns {:ok, nil} (propagates), not the old {:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, ...}}}. Eq/neq (==, !=) are explicitly stated as needing NO code change (plain Elixir == already propagates nil sensibly). Arithmetic's null-is-always-an-error disposition (§4.2 check 1, ahead of the type/promotion checks; §4.4) is unchanged from iteration 0. §4.5 now also states two concrete worked eval/2-level test cases matching AC5's own wording: (a) Expr.eval({:cmp, :lt, {:var, ["amount"]}, {:lit, 100}}, %{"amount" => nil}) -> {:ok, nil}; (b) Expr.eval({:arith, :add, {:var, ["amount"]}, {:lit, 1}}, %{"amount" => nil}) -> {:error, {:eval_error, {:null_in_arithmetic, :add, nil, 1}}}. These are now observably DIFFERENT eval/2-level outcomes (a value vs. an error), which is what makes AC5 satisfiable. §4.6 (equality/ordering involving infinity_marker()) was re-checked and now states the full 5-clause guard order for the ordering-comparison clause (nil-check, then :nan guard, then infinity-marker branch, then is_number guard, then type-mismatch fallback) with reasoning for why inserting the nil-check first cannot shadow the :nan/infinity branches (mutually exclusive operand shapes). §11's AC5 traceability row now points at the corrected §4.5/§4.6 content with the two worked test cases spelled out.
2. OQ-1 (§12, signed infinity/NaN 3-way split for float div/mod-by-zero, §4.3) -- carried forward UNCHANGED in substance, now with an explicit statement that ELIXIR-DEV must NOT implement §4.3's 3-way split until REVIEWER has given explicit sign-off (mirroring how REQ-191/REQ-192 escalated similar unverified-against-R-Co-source points), since R-Co's real src/expr/evaluator.zig remains confirmed unreachable from this sandbox (no *.zig file anywhere on this host).
3. OQ-4 (§12, negative-operand int div/mod rounding direction, §4.2 row A) -- carried forward UNCHANGED in substance, still flagged for REVIEWER's awareness only (not blocking): low-risk, reuses Elixir's native div/2 and rem/2 semantics with no new type/AST surface, no AC depends on it.
4. OQ-3 (§12, eval-time structured-error surface) -- relabelled only, no behavioural change: now stated plainly as a requirement-text-confirmed SCOPE EXCLUSION (the requirement's own SCOPE item 3 asks only for a parse-error surface, never an eval-time one), not an open question awaiting a future reader's resolution.

No other section was rewritten -- §2/§2.1/§2.2/§2.3, §3, §5, §6.1-§6.6, §7, §8, §9, §10 are unchanged from the version that already passed every other Step 1b check in the prior (FAILED-on-one-BLOCKER-only) pass.
acceptance_criteria: §4.5's revised ordering-comparison disposition genuinely resolves the BLOCKER: confirm eval/2's ordering-comparison clause is specified to return {:ok, nil} for a nil operand (checked ahead of is_number), and that this is stated as a real, deliberate behavioural change to expr.ex:437-446 -- not hedged back into an evaluate_condition/2-boundary-only reading.

AC5's two worked test cases in §4.5 are genuinely two DIFFERENT eval/2-level outcomes (one {:ok, nil}, one {:error, {:eval_error, {:null_in_arithmetic, ...}}}) -- re-verify this actually satisfies AC5's exact wording as read from docs/requirements.yaml, not from this handoff's paraphrase.

§4.6's re-checked guard ordering (nil-check, :nan guard, infinity-marker branch, is_number guard, type-mismatch fallback) is internally consistent and does not shadow or misorder against the pre-existing :nan/infinity-marker handling -- verify the mutual-exclusivity reasoning given (nil vs. :nan vs. infinity-marker are disjoint operand shapes) actually holds.
§11's AC5 traceability row points at the corrected §4.5/§4.6 content.

Eq/neq's 'no code change needed' claim in §4.5 is correct -- spot check that plain Elixir == on nil against another value or nil produces the stated results (nil == nil is true, nil == 5 is false) and that this genuinely satisfies the requirement's propagation framing for eq/neq without a new guard.

OQ-1 is carried forward as a genuine open question requiring REVIEWER's explicit sign-off before ELIXIR-DEV implements §4.3's 3-way infinity/NaN split -- confirm this gating language is present and unambiguous, not silently downgraded to 'awareness only'.
OQ-4 is carried forward as REVIEWER-awareness-only, non-blocking -- confirm it is not mistakenly escalated to blocking or merged with OQ-1's stronger gating language.

OQ-3 is correctly relabelled as a confirmed scope exclusion (matching the requirement's own SCOPE item 3 wording, parse-error surface only) rather than an open question -- no behavioural content should have changed here, wording only.

Re-confirm no other section was rewritten without cause -- diff-check that §2/§2.1/§2.2/§2.3, §3, §5, §6.1-§6.6, §7, §8, §9, §10 remain byte-identical (or near-identical, allowing only the §11 AC5 row edit) to the version that already passed those specific checks in the prior Step 1b pass.

Zero literal Elixir implementation code anywhere in the design doc -- grep for 'defmodule', 'def ', and a trailing bare 'end' outside a @type/@spec continuation; confirm every fenced block remains a @type/@spec declaration, BNF/table, or plain-English pseudocode, never a working function body.

CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (this file, top level, not nested under result) must be exactly one of PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish your pass -- grep the file yourself before finishing, and run mix letflow.lint_handoffs if available, per this project's own recurring anti-pattern entry on this exact mistake.
